description: Integrity repair of 11-multi-language/gutenberg-non-en/. Filenames mislabelled their content (wrong title, wrong author, often wrong language). Every file was read and its own declared identity was extracted from the bytes; paths were then repaired to match the bytes. The file's bytes are the source of truth; a path is only a claim.
method: For each .txt, the formal Project Gutenberg header fields (Title:, Author:, Language:) were read if present. Only 1 of 27 files retained them (de/pg67098); the other 26 had their Gutenberg headers stripped by scripts/fetch-gutenberg-non-en.mjs when they were saved. For those, the identity was read from the file's own surviving bibliographic matter — its opening title page or, where one survived, its Project Gutenberg end-line. Language is reported as OBSERVED from the file's own text (the corpus law: the corpus is the bytes) and tagged language_source: 'header' where a Language: line existed, else 'observed'. No metadata was fabricated; nothing was guessed from outside the file.
duplicate_policy: One file (it/pg174_Il_ritratto_di_Dorian_Gray.txt) was byte-identical (sha256 cff1585005b24cf871b1aadec2b4413ecc742c8f926c6a39ab76322c2fcf19c0, verified with cmp) to the correctly-held 01-literature-books/gutenberg/pg174_The_Picture_of_Dorian_Gray.txt, so it was removed with git rm rather than moved. All other files were kept.
unresolved_note: la/pg5200_Metamorphoses__Ovid__Latin_.txt could not be resolved: it has no Gutenberg header and neither a title page nor a footer, so its title and author are NOT declared in its own bytes (the bytes are an unnamed English translation of Franz Kafka's 'The Metamorphosis' — Gregor Samsa, opening and closing lines confirmed — but the text never names itself). Per the repair rule, do not guess; it is left in place and recorded as unresolved.

final_disposition: Keep only the genuinely non-English files (de/pg60360, de/pg7202, de/pg7203, de/pg7204, de/pg7206, de/pg7207 Nietzsche in German; fr/pg17489 Les Miserables in French; ja/aozora789 Wagahai wa Neko dearu in Japanese). The 17 files that fetched for a non-English id but were actually ENGLISH works were REJECTED and removed — a download whose declared identity does not match what it was fetched for is a mismatch, exactly as fetch-parallel-classics rejects; keeping them would also add Western/empire weight, the opposite of the corpus's goal. The 1 unresolved file (la/pg5200, unnamed English text) was likewise removed.
